summary.intent: Build a full interactive TUI dashboard for the memory-loop subsystem using Charmbracelet/bubbletea libraries, allowing users to browse, manage, and configure memories from a single interface.
summary.outcome: A 4-tab bubbletea TUI was implemented in a new `memorylooptui` package with Memories, Injection, History, and Settings tabs. Settings key handling was debugged and fixed, accent color changed to orange, borders/spacing improved iteratively, but the settings tab visual design still doesn't match the mockup at session end.

repo: The CLI uses a `termstyle` package for ANSI 256-color styling; color `8` (dark gray) is invisible on dark terminals — use `245` (light gray) for visible borders.
The project uses a `memoryloop` package under `cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/` with functions like `TransitionRecordLifecycle`, `SelectRelevant`, `AddManualRecord`, `PruneRecords`, `SaveState`.
The `docs/superpowers/` directory is gitignored, so spec/plan docs written there are not committed to the repo.
ACCESSIBLE=1 env var is already used by the CLI to simplify huh forms; the TUI falls back to plain-text show when this is set.
The project uses `go.mod` with charmbracelet libraries already available as dependencies.

code.finding: In the root model's Update method, the tea.KeyMsg case processes global keys then falls through — delegation to tab models at line ~175 uses the outer msg parameter (tea.Msg), not the typed tea.KeyMsg. Tab models must do their own type assertion. This is correct Go behavior but was a source of debugging confusion.
Settings key handling was broken when using pointer fields in settingsChangedMsg closures. Fix was to refactor to capture the full struct value rather than pointer fields, making changes synchronous.
Detail pane was hidden by default (showDetail: false). Changed to showDetail: true so it shows immediately without requiring Enter press.
Log table height must be capped (h - reservedLines) to prevent content overflow pushing the tab bar off-screen. Used h-10 initially but needed more aggressive reservation.

workflow: Visual companion (local HTTP server with HTML mockups) is valuable for design approval before implementation — prevents misalignment between spec and reality.
Subagent-driven development dispatched Tasks 1-3 together as one agent since they were tightly coupled foundational work; this was more efficient than one agent per task.
Debug logging to a temp file (/tmp/tui-debug.log) was the correct approach to trace bubbletea message routing issues since the TUI captures stdin/stdout.
lipgloss border color must be explicitly set to a visible color (245) — the default or color 8 renders as invisible on dark terminals.
The brainstorm visual companion server shuts down between sessions and must be restarted; content written to the brainstorm directory persists across restarts.

friction: Multiple iteration cycles needed for border visibility — lipgloss color `8` (dark gray) was used initially and was invisible on dark terminals, requiring re-discovery in multiple files.
Settings key handling required extensive debugging including adding file-based debug logging to trace bubbletea message routing.
maxWidth cap of 80 was too narrow for the user's terminal, causing layout issues that required removal.
Injection tab content overflowed terminal height and pushed the tab bar off-screen, requiring height capping fixes.
The brainstorm server stopped between user questions about 'how to use' and 'open visual companion again', requiring a restart.
Fix agents committed changes mid-session making it unclear which files had uncommitted changes in the main session.
open_items: Settings tab visual design still doesn't match the mockup — user noted 'its not as nice as this one' at session end; the mockup uses a single-panel row layout rather than bordered cards.
History tab `R` refresh trigger is a placeholder — async refresh via tea.Cmd is not yet wired to the actual memoryloop.Refresh function.
Injection tab prompt tester scoring — the match results display was implemented but the actual SelectRelevant integration needs verification.
No unit tests for the TUI package — the plan noted 'manual verification focus' and tests were explicitly deferred.
Async spinner state for refresh in History tab was noted in the design but marked as a future enhancement.
The `prune` action keybinding (`x` for archive vs prune distinction) was added in spec self-review but needs UX validation.
The spec and implementation plan files were written to `docs/superpowers/` which is gitignored — they exist only locally.
